subproblems.title: Truncated cone map: a Lipschitz H on ℝ^{n+1} that equals (s, u) ↦ s·G(u) near {0 < s < 1, ‖G(u)‖ < ρ}, with its derivative there
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), ρ ∈ ℝ, and let G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P (Euclid n → Euclid P) be L-Lipschitz. For z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} write z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0 and tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^n. Then there is a map H : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, Lipschitz with some constant K ≥ 0, such that for every z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ: (a) H(z) = z_0·G(tail z); and (b) if G is differentiable at tail z, then the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) of directional derivatives equals Fin.cons (G(tail z)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(tail z)e_a), i.e. DH(z)ê_0 = G(tail z) and DH(z)ê_{a+1} = z_0·DG(tail z)e_a for a ∈ Fin n. Here D = fderiv ℝ, ê_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : NNReal) (ρ : ℝ), LipschitzWith L G → ∃ H : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P, (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K H) ∧ ∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ < ρ → H z = WithLp.ofLp z 0 • G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) ∧ (DifferentiableAt ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) → (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)) = Fin.cons (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))) (fun a => WithLp.ofLp z 0 • fderiv ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1, 2, 3(a) and 4 of the selected parent proof (the cone parametrization H_i(s, u) = s·G_i(u)), stated for one Lipschitz map G and an arbitrary radius ρ. This parametrizes Simon's cone 0 ⨯ T = h_#([[(0,1)]] × T), h(t, x) = tx (Ch. 6, 2.30, chapter-06.txt lines 525–536).
Notation. π₀ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ, π₀(z) := z_0 (EuclideanSpace.proj 0), and π′ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^n, π′(z) := tail z. π′ is linear (additivity and homogeneity hold definitionally), so both are continuous linear maps (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap on the finite-dimensional ℝ^{n+1}) and hence Lipschitz with constants ‖π₀‖ and ‖π′‖. On the standard basis: π₀ê_0 = 1, π′ê_0 = 0, π₀ê_{a+1} = 0 and π′ê_{a+1} = e_a. This follows by comparing coordinates: (ê_b)_j = [j = b], Fin.tail shifts indices by Fin.succ, Fin.succ is injective and Fin.succ a ≠ 0.

1. (Radius.) Put ρ′ := max(ρ, 1). Then ρ′ > 0 and ρ′ ≥ ρ.
2. (Retraction.) Let φ be the ContDiffBump centered at 0 ∈ ℝ^P with rIn = ρ′ and rOut = ρ′ + 1 (valid since 0 < ρ′ < ρ′ + 1), and r(y) := φ(y)·y.
 (a) r is C¹, as the product of the smooth φ and the identity, and has compact support because φ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). Hence r is Lipschitz with some constant K_r (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport).
 (b) ‖r(y)‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 for all y. If ‖y‖ < ρ′ + 1, then ‖r(y)‖ = |φ(y)|·‖y‖ ≤ 1·(ρ′ + 1) since 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1. Otherwise dist(y, 0) ≥ rOut, so φ(y) = 0 (ContDiffBump.zero_of_le_dist) and r(y) = 0.
 (c) r(y) = y whenever ‖y‖ ≤ ρ′, because φ = 1 on closedBall(0, rIn) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall).
3. (Clamp.) σ(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)). σ is 1-Lipschitz (s ↦ min(s, 1) and t ↦ max(0, t) are 1-Lipschitz), 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1 so |σ(s)| ≤ 1, and σ(s) = s for s ∈ (0, 1).
4. (Definition.) H(z) := σ(z_0)·r(G(tail z)).
5. (H is Lipschitz.) Put f₁(z) := σ(π₀z) and f₂(z) := r(G(π′z)). f₁ is ‖π₀‖-Lipschitz with |f₁| ≤ 1, and f₂ is K_r·L·‖π′‖-Lipschitz with ‖f₂‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 (steps 2 and 3). For z, z′ ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, H(z) − H(z′) = (f₁(z) − f₁(z′))·f₂(z) + f₁(z′)·(f₂(z) − f₂(z′)). Hence
 ‖H(z) − H(z′)‖ ≤ |f₁(z) − f₁(z′)|·‖f₂(z)‖ + |f₁(z′)|·‖f₂(z) − f₂(z′)‖ ≤ ((ρ′ + 1)·‖π₀‖ + K_r·L·‖π′‖)·‖z − z′‖,
 so H is Lipschitz with constant K := ((ρ′ + 1)‖π₀‖ + K_r L ‖π′‖)₊ (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le').
6. (Local form; part (a).) Fix z with z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ. Let H̃(z′) := π₀(z′)·G(π′z′) and O := {z′ : π₀z′ ∈ (0, 1), ‖G(π′z′)‖ < ρ′}. O is open, as the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (0, 1) and (−∞, ρ′) under continuous maps (G is continuous because it is Lipschitz). z ∈ O because ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ ≤ ρ′. For z′ ∈ O, σ(z′_0) = z′_0 by step 3 and r(G(tail z′)) = G(tail z′) by step 2(c), since ‖G(tail z′)‖ < ρ′. So H = H̃ on the neighbourhood O of z, i.e. H =ᶠ[𝓝 z] H̃. In particular H(z) = z_0·G(tail z), which is (a).
7. (Derivative.) Assume G is differentiable at u := tail z. π₀ and π′ are continuous linear, so G∘π′ has derivative DG(u)∘π′ at z (chain rule). By the product rule (HasFDerivAt.smul), H̃ has at z the derivative D := z_0·(DG(u)∘π′) + π₀.smulRight(G(u)), that is D(v) = z_0·DG(u)(π′v) + (π₀v)·G(u). Since H =ᶠ[𝓝 z] H̃, DH(z) = DH̃(z) = D (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
8. (Evaluation on the basis; part (b).) From π₀ê_0 = 1 and π′ê_0 = 0 we get D(ê_0) = z_0·DG(u)(0) + 1·G(u) = G(u). From π₀ê_{a+1} = 0 and π′ê_{a+1} = e_a we get D(ê_{a+1}) = z_0·DG(u)e_a. By Fin.cases on b ∈ Fin (n+1) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ), the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) equals Fin.cons (G(u)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(u)e_a), which is (b). ∎

  have hρ'pos : 0 < ρ' := lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos (le_max_right _ _)
  obtain ⟨r, ⟨Kr, hKr⟩, hr_bound, hr_id⟩ : ∃ r : Euclid P → Euclid P, (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K r) ∧
      (∀ y, ‖r y‖ ≤ ρ' + 1) ∧ (∀ y : Euclid P, ‖y‖ ≤ ρ' → r y = y) := by
    let φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid P) := ⟨ρ', ρ' + 1, hρ'pos, by linarith⟩
    refine ⟨fun y => φ y • y, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have hr_smooth : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y : Euclid P => φ y • y) := φ.contDiff.smul contDiff_id
      have hr_supp : HasCompactSupport (fun y : Euclid P => φ y • y) := φ.hasCompactSupport.smul_right
      exact ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport hr_supp hr_smooth (by simp)
    · intro y
      by_cases hy : ‖y‖ < ρ' + 1
      · calc ‖φ y • y‖ = |φ y| * ‖y‖ := by rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs]
          _ ≤ 1 * (ρ' + 1) := by
            gcongr
            · rw [abs_of_nonneg φ.nonneg]; exact φ.le_one
          _ = ρ' + 1 := one_mul _
      · have h0 : φ y = 0 := φ.zero_of_le_dist (by simpa [dist_zero_right] using not_lt.mp hy)
        simp [h0]; linarith
    · intro y hy
      have : φ y = 1 := φ.one_of_mem_closedBall (by simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using hy)
      simp [this]

  obtain ⟨σ, hσ, hσb, hσid⟩ : ∃ σ : ℝ → ℝ, LipschitzWith 1 σ ∧ (∀ s, |σ s| ≤ 1) ∧
      ∀ s ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, σ s = s := by
    refine ⟨fun s => max 0 (min s 1), (LipschitzWith.id.min_const 1).const_max 0, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro s
      rw [abs_le]; constructor
      · have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ max 0 (min s 1) := le_max_left _ _
        linarith
      · exact max_le (by norm_num) (min_le_right _ _)
    · intro s hs
      simp only [min_eq_left hs.2.le, max_eq_right hs.1.le]
  -- coordinate maps `π₀ z = z₀`, `π' z = tail z`
  let π0 : Euclid (n + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ := EuclideanSpace.proj 0
  have hπ0 : ∀ z, π0 z = WithLp.ofLp z 0 := fun z => rfl
  let πtl : Euclid (n + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n :=
    { toFun := fun z => WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))
      map_add' := fun x y => rfl
      map_smul' := fun c x => rfl }
  let πt : Euclid (n + 1) →L[ℝ] Euclid n := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap πtl
  have hπt : ∀ z, πt z = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) := fun z => rfl
  -- step 2: the map `H(z) = σ(z₀) • r(G(tail z))`
  refine ⟨fun z => σ (WithLp.ofLp z 0) • r (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))), ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- step 3(a): `H` is Lipschitz
    have h1 : LipschitzWith (1 * ‖π0‖₊) (fun z : Euclid (n + 1) => σ (WithLp.ofLp z 0)) :=
      hσ.comp π0.lipschitzWith
    have h2 : LipschitzWith (Kr * (L * ‖πt‖₊))
        (fun z : Euclid (n + 1) => r (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))))) :=
      hKr.comp (hG.comp πt.lipschitzWith)
    refine ⟨_, LipschitzWith.of_dist_le' (K := (ρ' + 1) * ((1 * ‖π0‖₊ : NNReal) : ℝ) +
      ((Kr * (L * ‖πt‖₊) : NNReal) : ℝ)) fun z z' => ?_⟩
    have e1 := h1.dist_le_mul z z'
    have e2 := h2.dist_le_mul z z'

    set a' := σ (WithLp.ofLp z' 0)
    set R := r (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))))
    set R' := r (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z'))))
    have ha' : ‖a'‖ ≤ 1 := (Real.norm_eq_abs _).le.trans (hσb _)

          gcongr

        Ht z' := by
      rintro z' ⟨h0, hρz⟩
      rw [hπ0] at h0
      rw [hπt] at hρz
      show _ = π0 z' • G (πt z')
      rw [hπ0, hπt, hσid _ h0, hr_id _ hρz.le]
    have hev : (fun z' : Euclid (n + 1) =>
        σ (WithLp.ofLp z' 0) • r (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z'))))) =ᶠ[𝓝 z] Ht :=
      Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem (hO.mem_nhds hzO) hEq
    refine ⟨hEq z hzO, fun hGd => ?_⟩
    have hD : HasFDerivAt Ht (π0 z • (fderiv ℝ G (πt z)).comp πt + π0.smulRight (G (πt z))) z :=
      π0.hasFDerivAt.smul (hGd.hasFDerivAt.comp z πt.hasFDerivAt)
    rw [hev.fderiv_eq, hD.fderiv]
    have hs0 : π0 (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = 1 := by simp [π0]
    have hss : ∀ a : Fin n, π0 (EuclideanSpace.single a.succ 1) = 0 := by
      intro a; simp [π0, Fin.succ_ne_zero]
    have ht0 : πt (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = 0 := by
      rw [hπt]; ext j; simp [Fin.tail, Fin.succ_ne_zero]
    have hts : ∀ a : Fin n, πt (EuclideanSpace.single a.succ 1) = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 := by
      intro a; rw [hπt]; ext j; simp [Fin.tail]
    funext b
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun a => ?_) b
    · simp [hs0, ht0]
      rfl
    · simp [hss, hts]
      rfl
proof_key_steps: ρ′ := max(ρ, 1). Let r(y) := φ(y)·y, with φ the ContDiffBump with radii ρ′ < ρ′ + 1. Then r is Lipschitz (C¹ with compact support), ‖r‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 and r = id on closedBall(0, ρ′). The clamp σ(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)) is 1-Lipschitz, |σ| ≤ 1 and σ = id on (0, 1).
H(z) := σ(z_0)·r(G(tail z)) is Lipschitz, by the product estimate using the bounds on σ and r and the Lipschitz coordinate maps.
On the open set O = {z′ : z′_0 ∈ (0, 1), ‖G(tail z′)‖ < ρ′} ∋ z, H coincides with H̃(z′) := z′_0·G(tail z′), so H(z) = z_0·G(tail z).
By the product and chain rules and EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, DH(z)v = z_0·DG(u)(tail v) + v_0·G(u). Evaluating at ê_0 and ê_{a+1} gives Fin.cons (G(u)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(u)e_a).

subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (H : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (w : Euclid n → ℤ) (c : Euclid n → ℝ), Measurable G → MeasurableSet A → Measurable w → Measurable c → IntegrableOn (fun u => (w u : ℝ)) A → (∀ u ∈ A, ‖G u‖ ≤ ρ) → (∀ u ∈ A, 0 ≤ c u ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |α (fun a => fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))| ≤ c u * covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A → (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)) = Fin.cons (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))) (fun a => WithLp.ofLp z 0 • fderiv ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) → IntegrableOn (fun z : Euclid (n + 1) => (w (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) : ℝ)) {z : Euclid (n + 1) | WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A} ∧ (∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A → 0 ≤ WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), |α (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1))| ≤ WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∫⁻ z in {z : Euclid (n + 1) | WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A}, ENNReal.ofReal (|(w (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) : ℝ)| * (WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ρ * ∫⁻ u in A, ENNReal.ofReal (|(w u : ℝ)| * c u)

Source. Steps 3(c), 5, 6 and 7 of the selected parent proof, for one piece. Uses the siblings cyl_fubini (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini) and curry_le (the accepted cmcdt_lp_covector_curryLeft_norm_le).
Notation. ι(t, u) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) ∈ ℝ^{n+1} for t ∈ ℝ, u ∈ ℝ^n. Then ι(t, u)_0 = t and tail ι(t, u) = u (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, WithLp.ofLp_toLp). For an n-covector β, βDG(u)e denotes β(a ↦ DG(u)e_a).

0. (Preliminaries.) z ↦ z_0 and z ↦ tail z are continuous, hence measurable. u ↦ (w(u) : ℝ) is measurable, since every map out of the countable discrete ℤ is measurable (measurable_of_countable). By cyl_fubini applied to (n, A), B is measurable, and for every measurable f : ℝ^{n+1} → [0, ∞]
 ∫⁻_B f = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du.   (∗)
1. (Part (i).) h := w∘tail is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Apply (∗) to f(z) := ‖h(z)‖ₑ, so that f(ι(t, u)) = ‖w(u)‖ₑ: ∫⁻_B ‖h‖ₑ = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ‖w(u)‖ₑ dt du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ·vol((0, 1)) du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ du < ∞. Here vol((0, 1)) = 1 (Real.volume_Ioo), and the last integral is finite because w is integrable on A. So h is integrable on B.
2. (Covector identity.) For an (n+1)-covector α, x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and s ∈ ℝ:
 α(Fin.cons x (a ↦ s·v_a)) = (α.curryLeft x)(a ↦ s·v_a) = (∏_{a ∈ Fin n} s)·(α.curryLeft x)(v) = s^n·(α.curryLeft x)(v).
 The first equality is ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply (α.curryLeft x v = α(Matrix.vecCons x v), and Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons definitionally). The second is multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ).
3. (Part (ii).) Fix z ∈ B and put s := z_0 ∈ (0, 1), u := tail z ∈ A and v := G(u). Then c′(z) = s^n·‖v‖·c(u) ≥ 0, because s > 0, ‖v‖ ≥ 0 and c(u) ≥ 0. Let α be an (n+1)-covector. By the hypothesis on DH at z ∈ B and step 2,
 α(DH(z)ê) = α(Fin.cons v (a ↦ s·DG(u)e_a)) = s^n·(α.curryLeft v)(DG(u)e).
 Hence, using s^n ≥ 0, then the hypothesis on c at u applied to the n-covector α.curryLeft v, then curry_le (|α.curryLeft v| ≤ ‖v‖·|α|) together with c(u) ≥ 0:
 |α(DH(z)ê)| = s^n·|(α.curryLeft v)(DG(u)e)| ≤ s^n·c(u)·|α.curryLeft v| ≤ s^n·c(u)·‖v‖·|α| = c′(z)·|α|.
4. (Part (iii).) The function f(z) := ofReal(|w(tail z)|·c′(z)) is measurable, as a composition of products of measurable functions (G and c are measurable). By (∗),
 ∫⁻_B f = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} ofReal(|w(u)|·(t^n·‖G(u)‖·c(u))) dt du.
 Fix u ∈ A. Then c(u) ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ ‖G(u)‖ ≤ ρ, so in particular ρ ≥ 0. For t ∈ (0, 1) we have 0 ≤ t^n ≤ 1, hence |w(u)|·(t^n·‖G(u)‖·c(u)) ≤ |w(u)|·(1·ρ·c(u)) = ρ·(|w(u)|·c(u)), and ofReal(ρ·x) = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(x) because ρ ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Therefore the inner integral is at most ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) dt = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u))·vol((0, 1)) = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) (setLIntegral_mono, setLIntegral_const).
 Integrating over A (setLIntegral_mono, the right side being measurable) and pulling out the constant (lintegral_const_mul) gives
 ∫⁻_B f ≤ ∫⁻_A ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) du = ofReal(ρ)·∫⁻_A ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) du.
 (If A = ∅ both sides vanish; the inequality ρ ≥ 0 is only used at points u ∈ A.) ∎

subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P any map, H : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel, and w : ℝ^n → ℤ measurable with (w : ℝ) Lebesgue integrable on A. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) be a test form (TestFormOn univ (n+1): a smooth (n+1)-form with compact support) and let η be any n-form on ℝ^P (a map ℝ^P → Λ^n). Write z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0, tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)), and B := {z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} : z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and tail z ∈ A}. Assume:
(H1) for every z ∈ B, H(z) = z_0·G(tail z) and the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) equals Fin.cons (G(tail z)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(tail z)e_a);
(H2) for every u ∈ A, η(G u) = ∫_0^1 t^n·(ω(t·G u)).curryLeft (G u) dt, an interval integral of n-covectors; this is Kω(G u) for the radial homotopy operator K.
Then ∫_{u ∈ A} w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e_0, …, DG(u)e_{n−1}) du = ∫_{z ∈ B} w(tail z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê_0, …, DH(z)ê_n) dz. Here D = fderiv ℝ, e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^n, ê_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, and all measures are Lebesgue measure.

Source. Step 8(a)–(c) of the selected parent proof, for one piece. It is the parametrized form of the cone formula behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.30 (chapter-06.txt lines 525–536). With h(t, x) = tx, the computation in the proof of 2.27 (lines 468–476) reads h_#([[(0,1)]] × T)(ω) = ∫_0^1 ∫ ⟨ω(tx), x ∧ t^n T⃗(x)⟩ dμ_T(x) dt. Uses the siblings cyl_fubini (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini) and pullback_integrable (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_pullback_integrable).
Notation. ι(t, u) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, so that ι(t, u)_0 = t and tail ι(t, u) = u. DG(u)e := (a ↦ DG(u)e_a) and DH(z)ê := (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b). h(z) := w(tail z), and F(z) := h(z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê).

1. (h is integrable on B.) h is measurable (w is measurable as a map out of ℤ, and tail is continuous). By cyl_fubini (b) with f = ‖h‖ₑ, ∫⁻_B ‖h‖ₑ = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ‖w(u)‖ₑ dt du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ du < ∞, using vol((0, 1)) = 1 and the integrability of w on A. So h is integrable on B.
2. (F is integrable on B.) Apply pullback_integrable with Q := P, n := n+1, the L-Lipschitz map H, S := B, g := h and the test form ω. It shows that z ↦ h(z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê), which is F, is integrable on B.
3. (Fubini.) By step 2 and cyl_fubini (c), ∫_B F = ∫_{u ∈ A} ∫_{t ∈ (0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt du. Since A is measurable, it suffices (setIntegral_congr_fun) to prove for every u ∈ A that
 w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) = ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt.   (†)
 Fix u ∈ A and write v := G(u) and x := DG(u)e ∈ (ℝ^P)^n.
4. (Inner integrand.) Let t ∈ (0, 1) and z := ι(t, u). Then z_0 = t ∈ (0, 1) and tail z = u ∈ A, so z ∈ B. By (H1), H(z) = t·v and DH(z)ê = Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a). For every (n+1)-covector α, α(Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a)) = (α.curryLeft v)(a ↦ t·x_a) = t^n·(α.curryLeft v)(x) = t^n·α(Fin.cons v x). This uses curryLeft_apply_apply, with Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons, and multilinearity (map_smul_univ, ∏_{a ∈ Fin n} t = t^n). Hence
 F(ι(t, u)) = w(u)·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a)) = w(u)·(t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x)).
 Integrating over (0, 1) (setIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable (0, 1), then integral_const_mul) gives ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt = w(u)·∫_{(0,1)} t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt.
5. (The homotopy integral.) By (H2), η(v) = ∫_0^1 k(t) dt with k(t) := t^n·(ω(t·v)).curryLeft v. k is continuous. Indeed t ↦ ω(t·v) is continuous (ω is smooth), and β ↦ β.curryLeft v is continuous linear, being β ↦ (curryLeftLI β)(v) for the linear isometry curryLeftLI. So k is interval integrable on [0, 1]. Evaluation at the fixed tuple x, E_x(β) := β(x), is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). Hence, by ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm,
 η(v)(x) = E_x(∫_0^1 k) = ∫_0^1 E_x(k(t)) dt = ∫_0^1 t^n·((ω(t·v)).curryLeft v)(x) dt = ∫_0^1 t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt,
 again by curryLeft_apply_apply. Since 0 ≤ 1, the interval integral equals the integral over (0, 1] (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le), which equals the integral over (0, 1) because single points are null (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo).
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 4 and 5 give (†): w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) = w(u)·∫_{(0,1)} t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt. With step 3, ∫_A w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) du = ∫_A ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt du = ∫_B F, which is the claim. ∎

For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Fix n and a Borel set A ⊆ ℝⁿ.
1. (The splitting map.) Define e : ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ^{n+1} as the composite of four measurable equivalences: (i) the swap (u, t) ↦ (t, u) (MeasurableEquiv.prodComm); (ii) id × ofLp : ℝ × Euclid n → ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) (MeasurableEquiv.prodCongr (MeasurableEquiv.refl ℝ) (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).symm); (iii) the inverse of MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0, which sends (t, p) to Fin.insertNth 0 t p = Fin.cons t p (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove_symm_apply, Fin.insertNth_zero'); (iv) toLp : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → Euclid (n+1) (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)). Evaluating the composite, e(u, t) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) = ι(t, u). Being a composite of measurable equivalences, e is a measurable equivalence, in particular a measurable embedding, and its inverse is measurable.
2. (Measure preservation.) Each factor is measure preserving for the volume measures (volume on a product is the product measure): (i) by Measure.measurePreserving_swap; (ii) by MeasurePreserving.prod of MeasurePreserving.id and EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin n) (ofLp carries volume on Euclid n to the product Lebesgue measure on Fin n → ℝ); (iii) volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0 says piFinSuccAbove is measure preserving, hence so is its inverse (MeasurePreserving.symm); (iv) the inverse of the measure-preserving ofLp on Euclid (n+1) (EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin (n+1)) with MeasurePreserving.symm). By MeasurePreserving.comp, e is measure preserving from volume on ℝⁿ × ℝ (= volume ⊗ volume, Measure.volume_eq_prod) to volume on ℝ^{n+1}.
3. (Preimage of Â.) For (u, t) ∈ ℝⁿ × ℝ we have e(u, t)_0 = t and tail e(u, t) = u, so e(u, t) ∈ Â iff u ∈ A and t ∈ (0, 1). Hence e⁻¹(Â) = A × (0, 1).
4. (Part (a).) Since e is a bijection, step 3 gives Â = (e⁻¹)⁻¹(A × (0, 1)). The set A × (0, 1) is measurable (A Borel, (0,1) open) and e⁻¹ is measurable, so Â is Borel.
5. (Part (b).) Let f be Borel. subproblems.title: Interior product bound |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β| for the Euclidean coefficient norm (reuse of the accepted cmcdt_lp_covector_curryLeft_norm_le)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let v ∈ ℝ^N = Euclid N and let β be a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^N (Covector (Euclid N) (k+1)). Let ι_vβ := β.curryLeft v be the interior product, the k-covector ι_vβ(w_1, …, w_k) = β(v, w_1, …, w_k). Then |ι_vβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, where ‖v‖ is the Euclidean norm of v and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the values of α on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors.

Source: step 6 of the selected parent proof. That step rotates v to a basis vector f_{i₀}. It compares the Hilbert–Schmidt sums of ι_{f_{i₀}}β and β by the position at which the index i₀ occurs. The parent keeps only the tuples in which i₀ occurs exactly once. Here that count is written with the position sums R_p below. Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis).

Notation. ℝ^N = Euclid N with standard basis e. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{J strictly increasing} α(e∘J)²)^{1/2}. For an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^N indexed by Fin N and J : Fin m → Fin N, write f∘J := (f_{J(0)}, …, f_{J(m−1)}). For x ∈ ℝ^N, ι_xβ := β.curryLeft x is the k-covector w ↦ β(x, w_0, …, w_{k−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply: β.curryLeft x w = β (Matrix.vecCons x w), and Matrix.vecCons x w = Fin.cons x w). β.curryLeft is a continuous linear map in x, so ι_{cx}β = c·ι_xβ and ι_0β = 0.

1. (Homogeneity of the coefficient norm.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector γ: |c·γ| = |c|·|γ|. Each coefficient satisfies (c·γ)(e∘J) = c·γ(e∘J), so the radicand of |c·γ| is c² times the radicand X ≥ 0 of |γ|. Then √(c²·X) = √(c²)·√X = |c|·√X (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

2. (Case v = 0.) Then ι_vβ = 0, so |ι_vβ| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), and the right side ‖0‖·|β| = 0. Assume from now on v ≠ 0. Then N ≥ 1, since ℝ^0 = {0}. Put i₀ := 0 ∈ Fin N.

3. (Rotating v to a basis vector.) Put u := ‖v‖⁻¹·v. Then ‖u‖ = 1 and v = ‖v‖·u. The one-member family (u) indexed by the set {i₀} is orthonormal (a single unit vector), and finrank ℝ^N = N = card (Fin N). So Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^N indexed by Fin N with f_{i₀} = u. By linearity, ι_vβ = ‖v‖·ι_uβ. By step 1 and ‖v‖ ≥ 0, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ|. It therefore suffices to show |ι_uβ| ≤ |β|.

4. (Position sums.) For J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N put g(J) := β(f∘J)² ≥ 0. For each position p ∈ Fin (k+1) put R_p := Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} [J(p) = i₀]·g(J), where [·] is 1 if the condition holds and 0 otherwise.

5. (R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|².) (a, j) ↦ Fin.cons a j is a bijection Fin N × (Fin k → Fin N) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin N) (Fin.consEquiv). Under it the condition J(0) = i₀ becomes a = i₀, so R_0 = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} β(f∘Fin.cons i₀ j)². Since f∘Fin.cons i₀ j = Fin.cons f_{i₀} (f∘j) = Fin.cons u (f∘j) (Fin.comp_cons), each term equals (ι_uβ)(f∘j)². Hence R_0 = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} (ι_uβ)(f∘j)² = k!·|ι_uβ|², by sq_sum applied to the k-covector ι_uβ and the orthonormal basis f.

6. (R_p = R_0 for every p.) Let σ := Equiv.swap 0 p, the transposition of 0 and p in Fin (k+1) (σ is the identity if p = 0). Then σ⁻¹ = σ and σ⁻¹(0) = p. The map J ↦ J∘σ⁻¹ is a bijection of Fin (k+1) → Fin N (Equiv.arrowCongr σ (Equiv.refl _)). We have (J∘σ⁻¹)(0) = J(p). Also β(f∘J∘σ⁻¹) = sign(σ⁻¹)·β(f∘J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to β.toAlternatingMap), and sign(σ⁻¹) = ±1, so g(J∘σ⁻¹) = g(J). Substituting J ↦ J∘σ⁻¹ in R_0 gives R_0 = Σ_J [(J∘σ⁻¹)(0) = i₀]·g(J∘σ⁻¹) = Σ_J [J(p) = i₀]·g(J) = R_p. (This is the parent's remark that moving f_{i₀} to the front only permutes the arguments, so β(f_{I'}) = ±β(f_{i₀}, f_I).)

7. (Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J g(J).) Exchanging the finite sums gives Σ_{p ∈ Fin (k+1)} R_p = Σ_J c(J)·g(J), where c(J) := #{p ∈ Fin (k+1) : J(p) = i₀}. If c(J) ≤ 1, then c(J)·g(J) ≤ g(J) because g(J) ≥ 0. If c(J) ≥ 2, there are positions p ≠ q with J(p) = J(q) = i₀. Then the argument tuple f∘J has equal entries in the distinct slots p and q, so β(f∘J) = 0 because β is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq). Hence c(J)·g(J) = 0 = g(J). Summing over J proves the claim. (This is the parent's restriction to tuples in which i₀ occurs exactly once. Tuples containing i₀ twice contribute 0, and the dropped terms are ≥ 0.)

8. (Total sum.) Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} g(J) = (k+1)!·|β|², by sq_sum applied to the (k+1)-covector β and the orthonormal basis f.

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 5–8, (k+1)·k!·|ι_uβ|² = Σ_{p ∈ Fin (k+1)} R_p ≤ (k+1)!·|β|² = (k+1)·k!·|β|². Divide by (k+1)·k! > 0 to get |ι_uβ|² ≤ |β|². Both norms are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so |ι_uβ| ≤ |β|. With step 3, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, that is, covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β. ∎

Position sums R_p := Σ_{J(p) = i₀} β(f∘J)²: R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|² by Fin.cons reindexing and sq_sum.
R_p = R_0 by the transposition 0 ↔ p (sign² = 1).
Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J β(f∘J)² = (k+1)!·|β|², because tuples with i₀ in two slots vanish; cancel (k+1)·k! and take square roots.

DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Put F(z) := ω(H z)(DH(z)e) = ω(H z)(a ↦ DH(z) e_a).
1. (ω is bounded.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞), hence continuous, and has compact support. So there is M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M for all y ∈ ℝ^Q, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm of continuous alternating maps (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Since ‖ω(y)‖ ≥ 0, M ≥ 0.
2. (Derivative bound.) For every z ∈ ℝⁿ, ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; at points where H is not differentiable fderiv is 0). Hence, for each a, ‖DH(z) e_a‖ ≤ ‖DH(z)‖·‖e_a‖ = ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L, because ‖e_a‖ = 1.
3. (F is bounded.) By the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |F(z)| ≤ ‖ω(H z)‖·∏_a ‖DH(z) e_a‖ ≤ M·Lⁿ for all z (monotonicity of products of nonnegative factors).
